Information Note to the Press (Press Release No.127 /2026) 
TELECOM REGULATORY AUTHORITY OF INDIA 
New Delhi, 5 October, 2026 
For Immediate release Website:- www.trai.gov.in 
"The Indian Telecom Services Yearly Performance 
Indicators" for the year 2025-26 
TRAI today has released the "The Indian Telecom Services-Yearly 
Performance Indicators" for the year 2025-26. This Report provides a 
broad perspective of the Telecom Services in India and presents the kev 
parameters and growth trends of the Telecom Services as well as Cable TV, 
DTH & Radio Broadcasting services in India for the period covering 1� April 
2025 to 31� March 2026. This report is compiled mainly on the basis of the 
information furnished by the Service Providers. 
Executive Summary of the Report is enclosed. The complete Report is 
available on TRAI's website www.trai.gov.in and under the link http://www.
trai.gov.in/release-publication/reports/performance-indicators-reports. 
Any suggestion or any clarification pertaining to this report, Shri Vijay 
Kumar, Advisor (F&EA), TRAI may be contacted on Tel. +91-20907773 and 
e-mail: advfeal@trai.gov.in. 
79** 0 
(Harinder Kumar) 
Secretary, TRAI 
Page 1 of 11 
Page 2 of 11 
 
Executive Summary 
 
 
1. Total number of internet subscribers increased from 969.10 million at 
the end of March 2025 to 1092.79 million at the end of March 2026 with 
yearly rate of growth of 12.76%. Out of total 1092.79 million internet 
subscribers, number of broadband subscribers is 1065.88 million, and 
number of narrowband subscribers is 26.91 million at the end of     
March 2026. 
 
Composition of Internet Subscription as on 31st March 2026 
 
 
 
2. Number of Broadband subscribers increased from 944.12 million at the 
end of March 2025 to 1,065.88 million at the end of March 2026 with 
yearly rate of growth of 12.90%. The number of Narrowband subscribers 
also increased from 24.98 million at the end of March 2025 to 26.91 
million at the end of March 2026 with yearly rate of growth of 7.72%. 
 
3. Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) per month for wireless service 
increased from ₹174.46 in 2024-25 to ₹180.73 in 2025-26, thereby 
showing a yearly rate of growth of 3.59%. 
Page 3 of 11 
 
4. During the year 2025-26, the Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) per 
month for prepaid service was ₹190.66 and ARPU per month for 
postpaid service was ₹119.76*. 
 
5. During the year 2025-26, Average Total Minutes of Usage (MOUs) per 
subscriber per month were 950*. 
 
6. During the year 2025-26, the Minutes of Usage (MOUs) per subscriber 
per month for postpaid services were 305 * and for prepaid services were 
1055. 
 
7. Number of wireless data subscribers has increased from 939.51 million 
at the end of March 2025 to 1026.75 million at the end of March 2026 
with yearly rate of growth of 9.29%.  Further, total volume of wireless 
data usage also increased from 2,28,779 PB during the year 2024-25 to 
2,85,376 PB during the year 2025-26 with yearly growth of 24.74%. 
 
8. Total revenue from wireless data usage increased from ₹2,15,078 crore 
in the year 2024-25 to ₹2,39,874 crore in the year 2025-26 with yearly 
rate of growth of 11.53%. 
 
9. Average revenue realization per GB for wireless data usage decreased 
from ₹8.97 in 2024-25 to ₹8.02 in 2025-26 with yearly rate of decline 
10.59%. 
 
 
 
Note: *M/s Bharti Airtel Ltd. (BAL) was not including their M2M cellular subscriber base in their 
wireless (Mobile) subscriber base in earlier reports, while remaining operators were including their M2M 
Cellular subscriber base in their wireless (mobile) subscriber base. M/s BAL has now furnished its revised 
reports for FY 2025-26 including the M2M subscriber base and related indicators. The wireless subscriber 
base and related indicators have accordingly been calculated by incorporating revised reports of M/s BAL 
for FY 2025-26.  
 
Page 4 of 11 
 
10. Average Wireless Data Usage per wireless data subscriber per month 
increased from 21.53 GB 2024-25 to 25.51 GB in 2025-26 with yearly 
rate of growth 18.49% 
 
11. The total number of telephone subscribers in India increased from 
1,200.80 million at the end of March 2025 to 1,330.58 million at the 
end of March 2026, registering a yearly rate of growth 10.81%. The 
overall Tele-density in India increased from 85.04% at the end of March 
2025 to 93.26% at the end of March 2026 at yearly rate of growth 
9.66%. 
 
12. Telephone subscription in Urban Areas increased from 666.11 million at 
the end of March 2025 to 778.79 million at the end of March 2026 at 
the yearly rate of growth 16.92%. Urban Tele-density also increased 
from 131.45% at the end of March 2025 to 151.47% at the end of March 
2026 with yearly rate of growth of 15.23%.  
13. Rural telephone subscription increased from 534.69 million at the end 
of March 2025 to 551.79 million at the end of March 2026 at the yearly 
rate of growth of 3.20% and Rural Tele-density also increased from 
59.06% to 60.46% during the same period of time.  
 
 
Page 5 of 11 
 
Trend of Tele-density 
 
  
14. Out of the total telephone subscription, the shares of Rural telephone 
subscription decreased from 44.53% at the end of March 2025 to 
41.47% at the end of March 2026. The following chart depicts the rural-
urban market share of telephone subscribers for the four years. 
 
 
 
15. Out of 1,330.58 million total telephone subscribers, the number of 
Wireless (Mobile+FWA) Telephone subscribers is 1,282.33 million and 
the number of Wireline Telephone subscribers is 48.25 million at the 
end of March 2026. The following chart depicts the market share of 
Wireless and Wireline subscribers in India. 
Page 6 of 11 
 
Composition of Market Share Wireless & Wireline Subscribers 
 
 
 
16. Total Wireless (Mobile+FWA) subscribers increased from 1,163.76 
million  at the end of March 2025 to 1,282.33 million at the end of 
March 2026, thereby showing a yearly rate of growth of 10.19%1. During 
the year 2025-26, net addition of 118.58 million wireless subscribers 
was recorded.   
 
17. Overall Wireless (Mobile+FWA) Teledensity increased from 82.42% at the 
end of March 2025 to 89.88% at the end of March-26. Rural wireless 
Teledensity increased from 58.67% to 59.89% and Urban wireless 
Teledensity also increased from 124.83% to 143.10% at the end of March 
2026. 
 
18. Wireless (Mobile) subscribers increased from 1,156.99 million at the end 
of Mar-25 to 1,265.73 million at the end of March-26, thereby showing a 
yearly rate of growth of 9.40%*. During the year 2025-26, net addition of 
108.74 million wireless subscribers was recorded.   
 
 
1M/S Bharti Airtel Limited has started including their M2M cellular subscriber base in 
their wireless (mobile) subscriber base in FY 2025-26. As a result, there has been a 
significant increase in the wireless (mobile) subscriber base at the end of March 2026 .  
 

Page 7 of 11 
 
19. Wireless (Mobile) Teledensity increased from 81.94% at the end of March 
2025 to 88.71% at the end of March 2026. Rural wireless Teledensity 
increased from 58.40% at the end of March 2025 to 59.08% at the end 
of March 2026 and Urban wireless Teledensity also increased from 
123.99% to 141.30% during the same period of time. 
 
20. Total Wireline subscriber base increased from 37.04 million at the end 
of March 2025 to 48.25 million at the end of March 2026 with yearly 
rate of growth of 30.25%.   
 
21. Overall Wireline Tele-density increased from 2.62% at the end of March-
25 to 3.38% at the end of Mar-26. During the same period Rural 
wireline tele-density increased from 0.39% to 0.57% and Urban wireline 
tele-density also increased from 6.62% to 8.37%. 
 
22. Gross Revenue (GR) increased from ₹3,72,097 crore in the year 2024-25 
to ₹4,04,067 crore in the year 2025-26 with yearly rate of growth of 
8.59% and Applicable Gross Revenue (ApGR) also increased from 
₹3,56,283 crore to ₹3,81,645 crore with yearly growth rate of 7.12% 
during same period. Adjusted Gross  Revenue (AGR) increased from ₹ 
3,03,025 crore in the year 2024-25 to ₹ 3,34,659 crore in the year 2025-
26 with yearly rate of growth of 10.44%.  
 
23. Pass through charges decreased by 13.63% from ₹52,879 crore in the 
year 2024-25 to ₹45,673 crore in the year 2025-26. Pass-through 
charges as a percentage of Gross Revenue are 11.30% in 2025-26 as 
against 14.21% in the previous financial year. 
 
24. Spectrum Usage Charges (SUC) yearly increased by 6.12% from       
₹3,807 crore in the year 2024-25 to ₹4,040 crore in the year 2025-26 
and License Fee also increased by 10.40% from ₹24,242 crore to 
₹26,763 crore during the same period. 
 
Page 8 of 11 
 
 
Service wise composition of Adjusted Gross Revenue for the year 
2025-26 
 
 
 
25. Access services contributed 83.95% of the total Adjusted Gross Revenue 
of telecom services. In Access services, Gross Revenue (GR), Applicable 
Gross Revenue (ApGR), Adjusted Gross Revenue (AGR), License Fee (LF) 
and Spectrum Usage Charges (SUC) increased by 7.32%, 6.77%, 
10.85%, 10.84 and 6.26% respectively in the year 2025-26 over the 
previous year 2024-25. However, Pass Through Charges decreased by 
16.46% during the same period. 
 
26. A total of approximately 917 private satellite TV channels have been 
permitted by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB), as on 
31.03.2026, for uplinking only/downlinking only/both uplinking & 
downlinking. Out of 917 permitted satellite TV channels, 908 channels 
are available for downlinking in India.  
 
27. As per the reporting done by broadcasters in pursuance of the Tariff 
Order dated 3 rd March 2017 as amended, out of 908 permitted satellite 
TV channels which are available for downlinking in India, there are 342 
satellite pay TV channels as on 31 st March 2026. Out of 342 pay 

Page 9 of 11 
 
channels, 238 are SD satellite pay TV channels and 104 are HD satellite 
pay TV channels. Apart from these pay channels reported to TRAI, 
remaining 566 channels, permitted by MIB, are considered as Free-to-
Air (FTA) channels. 
 
28. During the period ending 31 st March 2026, there were 4 pay DTH 
service providers in India.  Pay DTH has net pay active subscriber base 
of around 49.05 million, as on 31 st March 2026 as compared to 56.92 
million subscribers, as on 31 st March 2025. This is in addition to the 
subscribers of the free DTH services of Doordarshan.   
 
29. Apart from the radio Stations operated by All India Radio, the public 
broadcaster, as on 31 st March 2025, there were 388 operational private 
FM Radio stations in 113 cities with operational 33 Private FM Radio 
broadcaster. As on 31 st March 2026, there are 390 operational private 
FM radio channels across 120 cities, operated by 31 private FM radio 
operators 
 
30. The advertisement revenue, as reported by FM Radio operators, 
decreased from ₹1818.71 crore in 2024-25 to 1616.42 in 2025-26.  
 
31. As on 31 st March 2026, 564 Community Radio stations are operational 
as compared to 531 Community Radio station, as on 31st March 2025.
